role: MainActor singleton that turns a CapabilityClassifier proposal into a session-sticky tier (Quick/Auto/Deep), owns the shared NaturalLanguage sentence embedder used by the classifier, keeps write-only routing counters, and enforces a 50/day Tier-3 turn cap. Also declares the per-conversation RoutingSessionState and the EmbeddingCentroid helper.
types: SmartProviderRouter: final class (@MainActor) — routing + embedder + Tier-3 cap
SmartProviderRouter.Tier: enum (Int, Comparable) — quick=1, auto=2, deep=3
RoutingSessionState: final class (@MainActor) — currentTier + turnCount per conversation, owned by AssistantViewModel
EmbeddingCentroid: enum — mean of embedding vectors
toplevel: Stored-property initializers: tierCounts/classifierProposalCounts start {quick:0, auto:0, deep:0}, stickinessOverrides 0, tier3CountByDay [:]; RoutingSessionState.turnCount = 0. The lazy embedders are separate units. Nothing persisted: the Tier-3 cap counter resets on every relaunch.

flags.text: Header says downgrades are allowed 'within the first 3 turns', but the caller increments turnCount before route() (AssistantViewModel+Routing.swift:120) and stickyTier tests turnCount < 3, so only turns 1 and 2 settle freely.
The adversarial Tier-3 daily cap lives only in memory (tier3CountByDay), so force-quitting the app resets the 50/day ceiling it is meant to enforce.

units.does: Orders tiers by rawValue (quick < auto < deep).

units.does: Classifies the message with CapabilityClassifier, applies sticky-tier rules against the session, bumps routing counters, logs the decision at .info and returns the chosen tier. Called only from AssistantViewModel routing's proposeTier in Auto mode, which increments turnCount before and stores the result as currentTier after.
Session stickiness: take the proposal if it is an upgrade, or during the settling window (turnCount < 3), or if it is Quick with no capability flags; otherwise keep session.currentTier.

returns proposed (capability-clear downgrade). Note proposed == .quick already implies requirement == .none per Requirement.requiredTier, so the second clause is redundant
falls through: returns session.currentTier (sticky)

flags.text: When the contextual embedder fails for one specific text, embed() falls back to the word-vector space for that text only. If this happens to a prototype phrase, EmbeddingCentroid averages vectors of different lengths into the centroid. If it happens to a query, cosineSimilarity returns 0 because the lengths differ, and the axis silently never fires for that message.
